===== CLAUDE.md =====

# MedChina — Monorepo

Prontuário inteligente e assistente clínico para Medicina Tradicional Chinesa. Derived from the flyee template (`template` git remote — pull base improvements with `/update-from-template`). This repo holds REAL business logic; the template conventions below still apply.

## Product (see docs/PRODUCT.md for the full PRD)

- **What it is**: clinical EHR + ambient AI assistant for TCM practitioners (acupuncture, auriculotherapy, moxibustion, cupping, Chinese dietary therapy). The practitioner keeps her attention on the patient; MedChina records, organizes and prepares the consultation for clinical review.
- **Core loop**: mobile app captures authorized consultation audio → transcription + speaker diarization → structured anamnesis auto-filled (with per-field provenance to the audio segment; absence never becomes negation) → gap/contradiction detection → (Pro) disharmony-pattern hypotheses, point/protocol suggestions and therapeutic-plan drafts — everything stays a draft until the professional reviews, edits, validates and signs.
- **Business model**: freemium. Gratuito (R$0, unlimited manual patients/records), Assistente (R$199/mo hypothesis, 3,000 min audio), Pro (R$299/mo hypothesis, 6,000 min + clinical reasoning). Trial Pro: 14 days or 300 min, no card, starting at the first OPERATIONAL action of any kind (recording, scheduling, import, library — migration `0084`, origin kept in `pro_trials.started_via`); it does NOT start at sign-up. Prices are launch hypotheses — keep them in configurable data, never hardcoded.
- **Platforms**: web (this repo, primary/complete) + companion mobile app (audio capture, voice notes, upload/status only — NO checkout/purchase in the app, store-policy rule).
- **MVP account model**: one workspace per professional (maps to the template's organizations; multi-professional clinics are post-MVP).
- **Safety language**: the AI never "diagnoses" — it prepares hypotheses/suggestions requiring validation. Red is reserved for risk/failure. See PRD §10 and §16.
- **Home page spec**: docs/HOME-SPEC.md (copy + composition, source of truth for the marketing home).

## Structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js 15 (App Router) + MUI v9 + MUI X Premium + Tailwind 4, deployed on Vercel. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - **Clinical core** (the MVP product, migration `0020_clinical.sql`): `/inicio` (app home: activation checklist + open drafts + recent records), `/pacientes` (list, `/novo`, `/[id]` record with alerts + timeline), `/consultas/[id]` (manual consultation: anamnesis blocks from `lib/anamnesis.ts` — one of them, cycle and fertility, conditional on the practice's declared area and the patient's mark, migration `0103` — autosave on blur, finalize, addenda). Post-signup lands on `/onboarding` — the **preparation of the practice** (revised 2026-10-12; it replaced the start choice of PRD §6.4 and a guided trail that walked a real consultation, after a user test in which the professional got lost when asked to start a consultation with no patient in the room): four steps that need NO patient — how she works (modalities, the five plus her own words, and areas), how she signs, recording ready, the next appointment. A consultation is a moment of use, so the first one is guided on `/consultas/[id]` itself (`FirstConsultationGuide`), never in the onboarding. The steps, the facts behind them and the home checklist live in `lib/onboarding.ts` and are read by all three surfaces (the flow, the home checklist, `/primeiros-passos`) with LIVE predicates (practice context / patient / finalized consultation), never click-tracking. **Two invariants the database enforces and the UI must keep honest**: a blank field is "não informado" (deleting the row, never storing a negative — PRD §10.5), and a finalized consultation is frozen (corrections are append-only addenda — PRD §8.5).
  - **Clinical library** (the out-of-consultation loop, `/biblioteca`): study chat grounded in the MTC collections with visible citations and a plan-configurable monthly quota; Pro case review over one patient's record (gated on the Pro entitlement, audited; no consent gate — `ai-processing` authorizes capturing the consultation, not rereading the record); deterministic pre-consultation briefing in the agenda/home; browsable acervo under the safeguards of `docs/LICENSING-LIBRARY.md`; and the professional's OWN protocols feeding the same RAG. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - **Product layer** (authenticated app, `app/(dashboard)`): screens are goal-first, never defaulted to CRUD tables. Reusable UX blocks in `components/product/*` (`EmptyState`, `OnboardingChecklist`, `ActivationProgress`, `SetupWizard`) backed by `packages/onboarding`. Quality is enforced deterministically, mirroring the marketing layer: the `product-screen` skill is loaded by a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) that also injects a digest of the product component catalog (`components/product/catalog.json` — the shape-conformance check: which shared component or not-yet-packaged template pattern covers the value being rendered, so a series/ratio/counter-set never ships as a sentence of numbers), a `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/product-lint.mjs`) checks every written file against the product contract (no raw theme values, a11y names on icon controls/labels/switches, error-never-rendered-as-empty, no GSAP), and flows are verified end-to-end with the `product-verify` skill (walks the real journeys — dead ends, lost context, error≠empty, leftover demo surfaces — before a screen is declared done). The template's demo dashboards/sample apps were removed; the UI showcase (`/ui`) and docs stay as a dev reference and should be pruned before launch.
  - **Platform layer**: server-gated superadmin area at `app/(dashboard)/admin` (`profiles.is_superadmin` + RLS; layout gate + superadmin-only menu group) with consoles for real metrics (`admin_metrics()` RPC), organizations & users (suspend kill-switch; ban, 2FA visibility and 2FA reset via service role; granting the superadmin role — migration 0096; permanent account deletion with ALL its data — migration 0099, see `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`), billing, AI, knowledge, audit (audit trail + sign-in access log + WhatsApp), **data insights** (ask the database in plain language; the model's SQL runs in a Postgres `READ ONLY` transaction and is shown with the answer), **backups** (`packages/backup`), announcements, help center, blog, **support** (`/admin/support` — quick-support widget channels stored in `platform_settings`, migration 0018) **live events** (`/admin/eventos` — each event with its own page copy, registrations, one-at-a-time 1:1 list, reminder e-mails and results; create, duplicate, archive; migrations 0112/0113) and **leads** (`/admin/leads` — one row per person across events: consent, opt-out, LGPD erasure and the consented ad-audience export, scoped by event). Account plumbing is real, not mock: header notification bell (`notifications` table + `lib/notifications.ts`), dismissible system announcements, profile/account settings (avatar storage bucket), floating quick-support widget reading `platform_settings` ('support' key, superadmin-managed) with `BRAND.support` as static fallback (hidden until a human channel is set).
  - **Marketing layer**: public site at `app/(marketing)` with Portuguese slugs (home, /como-funciona, /recursos, /planos, /seguranca, /migracao, /sobre, /contato, /ajuda, /blog, /legal — /ajuda and /blog serve DB-managed content written in the admin consoles, locale-aware with EN fallback via `lib/public-content.ts`) built from `components/marketing/*` primitives (Section/Container/SectionHeader/Reveal + premium archetypes: FeatureRows/BentoGrid/StatBand/ProductFrame/DataVizPlaceholder), GSAP motion, per-page SEO + sitemap/robots. The committed visual direction is persisted in `docs/DESIGN.md` and is STRICT (inherited by every new page/edit/section; redesign only on explicit request). Quality is enforced deterministically: a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads the `marketing-page` skill and injects a digest of the component catalog (`components/marketing/catalog.json`), and a `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/marketing-lint.mjs`) checks every written file against the marketing contract (tokens, i18n, icon alias, SEO, library composition). Site identity centralized in `apps/web/src/brand.ts`. Landing DS pages with their own chrome live in sibling route groups the marketing hooks do not watch: `(funil)` (offer/campaign/event pages, `noindex` — including the live events `/lei-15345` and `/ao-vivo/<slug>`, one template whose copy is written in `/admin/eventos`, `docs/PAGINA-EVENTO.md`) and `(autoridade)` (permanent, indexed — `/china`, `docs/PAGINA-CHINA.md`).
- `packages/design-tokens` — design system source of truth (CSS tokens + generated TS mirror). MedChina locks a SINGLE brand palette written into `css/green.css` (Teal `#177c81` primary / Camel `#c09362` secondary, exact brand values; derived accents jade/slate-blue/terracotta/plum) plus warm Parchment-tinted neutrals in `css/common.css`; the other theme files stay for template merges but are not loaded. Includes `css/marketing.css` (fluid display type scale, section rhythm, motion tokens). See `packages/design-tokens/README.md`.
- `packages/db` — Drizzle schema + SQL migrations with RLS (multi-tenant: organizations/memberships/invites — one workspace per professional in the MVP). See `packages/db/README.md`.
- `packages/auth` — Supabase auth clients (browser/server/middleware). Degrades gracefully when Supabase env vars are absent. 2FA (TOTP): enroll at `/settings/security`; the middleware forces the AAL2 step-up at `/auth/two-factor` for enrolled users. Also owns the **parallel session cookie** used by support impersonation (`authCookieName`): the operator's own session is never overwritten, and every client entry point resolves which cookie holds the active session from one marker — see `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
- `packages/email` — Resend + React Email templates (server-only). ACTIVE at launch (needs `RESEND_API_KEY`); no-ops without it and callers must offer a fallback.
- `packages/billing` — ACTIVE: per-org subscriptions (Gratuito/Assistente/Pro + minute credits), coupons, trials; Stripe + Asaas behind one `PaymentProvider` interface. Superadmin console at `/admin/billing`; customer page at `/settings/billing`. The MedChina plan catalog and the audio-minutes/Pro-trial layer on top of it live in migration `0024_trial_minutes.sql` (see `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`): the trial is NOT `plans.trial_days` (that is the provider's checkout trial) — it is card-less, starts at the first operational action of any kind (migration `0084` broadened `0024`), and ends on 14 days OR 300 minutes. See `packages/billing/README.md`.
- `packages/documents` — ACTIVE: issued documents with versioning, sha256 hash and QR-verifiable codes (public page `/verify/[code]`); PDF rendering is pluggable (caller supplies bytes). Issued docs are revoked, never deleted. Powers therapeutic plans/prescriptions with professional signature. See `packages/documents/README.md`.
- `packages/jobs` — Inngest client + typed event map for background jobs/cron. Functions live in the owning package's `src/jobs.ts`; all are served by `apps/web` at `/api/inngest`. `sendEvent` never throws — callers must fall back to inline processing. See `packages/jobs/README.md`.
- `packages/audit` — ACTIVE (compliance is core for clinical data): append-only `audit_events` (call `recordAudit` from `apps/web/src/lib/audit.ts` on every mutation), `access_events` sign-in trail, immutable row versioning — MedChina must enable it on clinical tables as they are created (`select public.enable_row_versioning('public.<table>')`), versioned consent terms + acceptances (patient consent for recording/AI is a product pillar). See `packages/audit/README.md`.
- `packages/backup` — automatic logical backups of every `public` table, nightly via Inngest plus on-demand from `/admin/backups`. See `packages/backup/README.md`.
- `packages/connectors` — NOT active at launch (kept inert for template merges). See `packages/connectors/README.md`.
- `packages/knowledge` — ACTIVE: knowledge base with trust levels + pgvector RAG (clinical library: traditional sources, internal protocols, scientific evidence — classified separately per PRD §9.9); Gemini embeddings; ingestion via Inngest with inline fallback. Superadmin console at `/admin/knowledge`. See `packages/knowledge/README.md`.
- `packages/ai` — ACTIVE: instruction-driven assistants (superadmin-managed) behind a `ChatProvider` interface (Anthropic/Gemini/OpenRouter), attachments, credits per message. Console at `/admin/ai`. The clinical AI pipeline (anamnesis filling, hypotheses) builds on this + `packages/transcribe` + `packages/knowledge`; each clinical feature is routed by its own env vars (`apps/web/src/lib/ai-routing.ts`: `EXTRACTION_*`, `HYPOTHESES_*`, `PLAN_*`, `SUMMARY_*`, `ATTACHMENT_*`), Gemini by default and the extraction's floor when another provider fails with pipeline time left (≥ 15 s; otherwise the recording is retried and the next attempt gets the floor) — the resolved routing shows in `/admin/ai` → Roteamento clínico, the switch checklist is in `docs/DEPLOY.md`. See `packages/ai/README.md`.
- `packages/transcribe` — ACTIVE (heart of the product): audio → diarized transcript (speakers + timestamps) via Gemini; Inngest job with inline fallback; optional source-audio deletion once the transcript is validated (PRD §14.3). See `packages/transcribe/README.md`.
- `packages/whatsapp` — INBOUND ONLY, for one job: **confirming the professional's WhatsApp at sign-up** (migration `0122`). Three rules: the NUMBER is mandatory, always (the form asks; a trigger on `auth.users` refuses an account without one); CONFIRMING it is an operator switch (`/admin/support` → `platform_settings.signup`, born OFF — until it is on, the sign-up is confirmed by e-mail only and nobody is held); with the switch on, an ordinary sign-up confirms BEFORE the account exists, while a campaign sign-up (headed to a checkout) is created at once, born pending, and confirms AFTER the payment (the middleware holds it at `/auth/whatsapp`). The confirmation is reversed: she sends a code from her own WhatsApp to `WHATSAPP_SIGNUP_NUMBER` and the Meta webhook confirms it. Nothing else sends through this package — patient-facing WhatsApp stays a `wa.me` handoff. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` (Auth) and `packages/whatsapp/README.md`.
- `apps/mobile` — ACTIVE: Expo (SDK 57) + expo-router + React Native Paper companion app (audio capture, voice observations, upload queue, processing status — no checkout, per store policy and PRD §4.4). Same identity as web (tokens → Paper themes, shared copy via `packages/content`, auth via `@flyee/auth/native`). Screen playbook: `.claude/skills/mobile-screen`. See `apps/mobile/CLAUDE.md`.
- `packages/fields` — pure validators/formatters/masks for semantic form fields (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, currency; persist digits, never masks) + `AddressLookupProvider` interface with ViaCEP as the built-in BR provider (lookup failure degrades to manual entry, never blocks the form). Zero deps, shared web/mobile; the MUI field components live in `apps/web/src/components/product/fields/`. See `packages/fields/README.md`.
- `packages/onboarding` — ACTIVE: activation mechanism behind the home checklist (prepare the practice → first patient → first finalized consultation) and the preparation flow's stored answers; step definitions live in this repo's code (`apps/web/src/lib/onboarding.ts`). See `packages/onboarding/README.md`.
- `packages/content` — cross-platform site identity (`BRAND`) + i18n message catalogs (`messages/{de,en,es,fr,pt-BR,zh-CN}.json`; **pt-BR is the default and the only search-indexed locale**), consumed by web (next-intl) and mobile (use-intl). Brand master art lives in `packages/content/brand/`.
- `attachments/` — input inbox: drop project material here (brand art, page imagery, briefs); agents route each file to its canonical home per `attachments/README.md` and the folder trends back to empty.

## Golden rules

- Visual identity (colors, themes, shadows, radii) changes ONLY in `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css`. Never hardcode theme values in an app.
- After changing token CSS, run `npm run tokens:generate` and commit the updated `tokens.generated.ts` together.
- Apps never import from other apps (`apps/web` ↛ `apps/mobile` and vice versa); shared code lives in `packages/*`.
- npm workspaces: always install dependencies from the root (`npm install`), never inside an app.
- Icons: Phosphor set via the tsconfig alias (`@/icons/nexture/*` → `src/icons/phosphor/*`; fallback stubs re-export Nexture — replace incrementally).
- Display font: TT Chocolates (commercial, `apps/web/src/fonts/tt-chocolates/`, weights 500/700/800 wired as `--font-display` in the root layout).
- Clinical safety: AI output is always a draft for professional review; never word UI/copy as autonomous diagnosis/prescription; red only for risk/error; prices/limits come from configurable data.

## Shared Claude/Codex harness

- `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/*/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/hooks/*` are the canonical shared sources. Do not maintain a second hand-written Codex copy.
- Codex reads the generated `AGENTS.md` mirror and generated `.agents/skills/*` discovery bridges. `.codex/config.toml` points its lifecycle hooks at the same implementations under `.claude/hooks/`.
- `PostToolUse` automatically runs `scripts/sync-agent-harness.mjs` after canonical harness edits. `npm run harness:check` and `npm run harness:test` are also enforced by the pre-commit hook.

## Commands (root)

- `npm run dev` / `build` / `lint:fix` — delegate to `apps/web`
- `npm run dev:mobile` — Expo dev server for `apps/mobile`
- `npm run typecheck` — both apps, each with its own pinned TypeScript (web 5.8 / mobile 6.0 — never run a bare root `npx tsc` on apps/web: it picks the hoisted TS 6)
- `npm run tokens:generate` — regenerate the TS token mirror

## Platform (confirmed decisions)

- Deploy: Vercel. Database/auth/storage: Supabase (Postgres + RLS, Auth, Storage; pgvector for RAG). ORM: Drizzle (`packages/db`).
- Billing: Stripe/Asaas behind an interface (`packages/billing`). Email: Resend + React Email (`packages/email`). Jobs/cron: Inngest (`packages/jobs`). AI: Anthropic/Gemini behind a provider interface (`packages/ai`); transcription/diarization via Gemini (`packages/transcribe`).
- Locale: pt-BR default (cookie-based i18n — crawlers index ONLY pt-BR); other locales (de,en,es,fr,zh-CN) available via the in-app switcher. Chinese is Simplified (`zh-CN`); the brand faces carry no Han glyphs, so the platform CJK families are appended to every font stack in `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts` (no webfont).
- Do not reintroduce Cloudflare-specific services (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI).

This repo stays **private**: the UI layer contains commercially licensed template code (MUI X Premium license) plus the commercial TT Chocolates font.

===== apps/web/CLAUDE.md =====

# MedChina Web (apps/web)

Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 — the MedChina platform (web is the primary, complete surface; see root CLAUDE.md and docs/PRODUCT.md).

## Stack and conventions

- **UI**: MUI v9 is the base — before building a component from scratch, check for an existing MUI or MUI X equivalent (DataGrid Premium, Charts Pro, Date Pickers Pro, Tree View are already installed). Icons: **Phosphor** via the `@/icons/nexture/*` tsconfig alias (16 real adapters; the rest are Nexture fallback stubs — replace incrementally, see `src/icons/README.md`).
- **Styling**: MUI theme driven by CSS variables (`hsl(var(--token))`) defined in `@flyee/design-tokens`. MUI component overrides live in `src/style/**/*.css` (organized by category), inside CSS layers (`theme, base, mui, components, utilities`). Tailwind 4 only for layout utilities; classes merged with `tailwind-merge`.
- **Themes**: SINGLE locked brand palette (Teal/Camel, written into `@flyee/design-tokens` `css/green.css`) × light/dark, applied via classes on `<html>` (`theme-green dark`) by the `ThemeProvider` (`src/theme/theme-provider.tsx`). `THEME_OPTIONS` holds only GREEN; the color switcher is removed. Display font: TT Chocolates (`src/fonts/tt-chocolates/`, `--font-display` in the root layout).
- **Forms**: Formik + Yup.
- **i18n**: next-intl — every UI string goes through messages, never hardcoded. Locales: `de,en,es,fr,pt-BR,zh-CN`; catalogs live in `packages/content/messages/` (shared with apps/mobile — the mobile app itself still ships the five it generates). Key parity across all six is pinned by `src/lib/import/messages.test.ts`. Namespaces: `marketing` (public site), `auth` (sign-in/sign-up/recovery/2FA), `product` (clinical app + onboarding), `dashboard` (chrome/menu). Admin consoles are the exception in the other direction: hardcoded **pt-BR**, no namespace (see the superadmin bullet).
- **Which language a request is in** is answered in ONE place: `lib/locale-request.ts` (`resolveRequestLocale`), used by both `i18n/request.ts` and any page that must say WHY it is in that language. The cookie is the visitor's own choice and always wins; without one, `lib/locale-detection.ts` decides from `Accept-Language`, falling back to Vercel's `x-vercel-ip-country`. Three rules are load-bearing: **(1) detection happens at RENDER time, not only in the middleware** — a cookie the middleware sets lands on the RESPONSE, so trusting it alone served the first page in Portuguese and switched only on the next navigation; the middleware persists the same decision so it survives and can be overridden. **(2) A crawler is never switched** (`isCrawler`) — i18n is cookie-based, so only `DEFAULTS.locale` is indexable (`docs/SEO.md`), and serving another language on the same URL would index content no URL can return; this also keeps link previews in the sharer's language. **(3) An automatic switch is always announced**: `COOKIE_KEYS.localeAuto` marks a locale the site chose, the public home renders the way back to Portuguese while it is set, and choosing or dismissing clears it. The locale cookie is written with a one-year max-age — as a session cookie, a choice died on browser close and detection overrode it on the next visit.
- **Path alias**: `@/*` → `./src/*`.
- **Brand**: site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicon paths) comes from `@flyee/content` (`src/brand.ts` is a re-export shim); the logo is the single component `src/components/logo/logo.tsx` (used by admin AND marketing chrome).

## Marketing layer (public site)

- Routes live in `src/app/(marketing)/` with Portuguese slugs (home `/`, `/como-funciona`, `/recursos`, `/planos`, `/seguranca`, `/migracao`, `/sobre`, `/contato`, `/ajuda`, `/blog`, `/legal/{termos,privacidade,cookies}`) with their own chrome — no admin layout. Each new public route must be added to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` (`src/middleware.ts`), and an INDEXED one to `src/app/sitemap.ts` too (the `noindex` landing pages stay out, named in its exclusion comment). The home is built section-by-section from `docs/HOME-SPEC.md` (contractual order); MedChina copy guardrails live in `docs/DESIGN.md` (never imply autonomous diagnosis; no unproven metrics/testimonials; prices are hypotheses from configurable data).
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` render DB-managed content (superadmin writes it in `/admin/help` and `/admin/blog`) through `src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows only, locale with EN fallback); the sitemap includes their published slugs and degrades to the static list without Supabase env. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx` (react-markdown, raw HTML ignored).
- **The home is multilingual** (2026-09-18): its copy lives in `src/components/marketing/home-copy/<locale>.ts` — six typed files, not the next-intl catalogs, because the page's content is structured arrays and per-slug records rather than flat keys. `pt-BR.ts` is the structural source of truth (`HomeCopy = typeof homeCopyPtBR`), so a key added, renamed or dropped there breaks the other five at COMPILE time. The server page picks one language and hands it down as a prop (the home is a client component: importing all six would ship six copies of the page to every visitor). Headlines keep their emphasis inline — `**accent**` → `<em>`, `__lead__` → `<strong>`, `==term==` → `<mark>`, `\n` → `<br>` (`home-copy/rich.tsx`) — so a translator never edits JSX and each language breaks its own lines. Structural choices (which icon, which screenshot, a field's review tone) stay in the component, keyed by id, so a translation can never move a screenshot or repaint a review state. The switcher (`home-language-switch.tsx`) writes the same cookie the logged-in switcher writes; the CJK families are appended to the landing font stacks via `--cjk` in `clinical-source-home.css`, because neither brand face has Han glyphs.
- **Two design systems** (`docs/DESIGN.md` scope note, revised 2026-08-11): **landing/offer/campaign pages** (the home, `app/(funil)/*`, `app/(autoridade)/*`) are built in the **Landing DS** — the `clinical-source-home.css` global class vocabulary, direct Phosphor imports, hardcoded pt-BR copy (the home excepted, above); **informational pages** compose the primitives in `src/components/marketing/` (`Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader`; Hero, FeatureGrid, PricingSection) — never hand-tuned spacing/widths. `marketing-lint` picks the contract by path — and only sees `app/(marketing)/**` and `components/marketing/**`: a Landing DS page inside `(marketing)` is blocked, and the sibling groups are never linted (their page spec is the checklist). See that folder's README and the `marketing-page` skill (load it before building/editing public pages — yourself, in the groups the hook does not watch).
- **Where a landing page lives** (2026-09-26): a page with its own chrome is a sibling route group with its own layout, never `(marketing)` behind a `body:has()` hack. `(funil)` holds offer, campaign and event pages (no site menu, `noindex`, out of the sitemap — FUNIL D10). `(autoridade)` holds permanent, INDEXED landing pages that wear the home's header and footer (`components/marketing/home-header.tsx`, `home-footer.tsx`, `home-brand.tsx`, extracted from the home for this) and the site-wide `SiteJsonLd`: today `/china` (`docs/PAGINA-CHINA.md`), whose content constants — including a publication date that must be the real one on deploy — live in `china-content.ts`. Blocks both groups use (`.offer-section--tinted`, `.offer-founder*`) are in `app/landing-shared.css`, imported by both layouts between the DS stylesheet and the group's own.
- **Live events — `/lei-15345` and `/ao-vivo/<slug>`** (migrations `0112_leads.sql` + `0113_live_events_crud.sql`, `docs/PAGINA-EVENTO.md` §18): ONE template (`(funil)/components/live-event-view.tsx`) renders every event from its `live_events` row — the page copy (headline with `**accent**`, byline, lead and its past-tense version, up to three topics from a fixed icon set, audience, link description) is DATA written in `/admin/eventos`, so a new event is a console action, not a deploy; the first event keeps `/lei-15345` (`LEGACY_EVENT_PATHS` in `lib/live-event-common.ts`, which `/ao-vivo/lei-15345` redirects to). One URL per event is the invitation, the room and the recording, driven by `state` (`rascunho` → 404 except a superadmin preview · `inscricoes` · `ao_vivo` · `encerrado`, where a per-event `ended_behavior` keeps the recording or redirects to an INTERNAL path — the CHECK refuses `//host` and absolute URLs; the console and the render both refuse the event's own page in any spelling, a draft and another redirecting event, a redirect the render skips is flagged to the superadmin on the page, and the recording e-mail is off while an event redirects). A draft's sign-up answers exactly like a missing event (no slug oracle); `page_title` and `offer_angle` (which `/assinar` opening the CTA's `utm_content` leads with) are per event. A partner has no record of her own: she is named in the event's byline and copy. Load-bearing rules: **(1) people with no account are LEADS, not users** — `leads` (one row per phone, 11 digits) and `live_event_registrations`, written ONLY by `submit_live_event_registration` (service role, behind the server action's honeypot and a per-network hourly window over `sha256(salt + IP)`), and a repeat NEVER rewrites name or e-mail (the confirmation shows the TYPED name, so nothing leaks about whoever owns the number). A form post does not prove the number is the typist's, so a registration for ANOTHER event never lifts an opt-out the team recorded, never re-grants a revoked news consent (it may add it only to someone who never had it), and its confirmation e-mail goes to a NEW person or only when the typed address equals the stored one; the per-network window counts THIS event's registrations. **(2) Consent is two versioned terms pinned on the row** (id + version + text snapshot): `evento-contato` (required, by submitting) and `medchina-novidades` (optional box, unticked; the only door to the ad audience). `consent_acceptances` needs an org, which a lead does not have. **(3) The personal link is the identity**: a 32-byte token, only its sha256 stored (`live_event_tokens`), kept in ONE httpOnly cookie with one `<slug>~<token>` entry per event, up to six events, newest first (`parseEventCookie`/`addEventToken` — one slot per browser made a second registration erase the first, and one slot per TOKEN let one event's e-mail links, each minting a token, push the other events out; a new token of the same event replaces its old one), and shown back as a link + QR (the QR opens the group ON THE PHONE, which has no cookie) — re-shown after a reload from the cookie itself. `/api/public/evento/*` (`entrar`, `grupo`, `whatsapp`, `presenca`, `estado`, `descadastrar`) never assume WHICH event: the token says it (`?i=`), or `?e=<slug>` names it for the cookie, and a request with neither (an old link, a tab opened before a deploy) falls back to the cookie's newest event (`lib/live-event-route.ts` `resolveRegistration`); they answer `no-store` + `no-referrer`, and the group invite and owner phone never reach the HTML. **(4) Presence is attendance at the LIVE**: the room's heartbeat (60 s, the server credits ≤ 120 s per beat) is refused unless the event is `ao_vivo`, and the recording sends none. **(5) After the live the promise is the recording**: the capture form, the confirmation, the WhatsApp message and the e-mail all switch (a post-event registration gets the recording e-mail, never "seu lugar está garantido"). **(6) E-mail is redundant, never blocking**: `lib/live-event-email.ts` sends per-kind batches (`resend.batch`, 100 at a time, `List-Unsubscribe`), marks only accepted items, and the Inngest job (`medchina/live-event.email`) falls back inline. **(7) Retention**: a daily cron (`purge_expired_leads`) erases leads six months after their last event unless the news consent is active; `purge_lead(lead, reason)` erases one on request — rows, tokens, presence AND their `record_versions`, audited with the reason only. **(8) Results are counted without personal data**: visits per event/day/channel only on a DOCUMENT load (`Sec-Fetch-Dest: document` — Next strips its own `RSC`/`Next-Action` headers from `headers()`, and the sign-up's action and refresh would otherwise count as two more visits), never for crawlers, drafts or superadmins (`count_live_event_view`, service role), with the channel spelled once for visits and registrations (`live_event_channel` / `normalizeChannel`) and at most 30 channels per event per day (the rest is "outro" — the query string is attacker-controlled); phone vs computer of the group click as a per-event COUNTER (`live_event_device_clicks`, bumped on a registration's first click), never a column on the person, whose contact term does not list it; and purchases in `purchase_attributions`, written by the billing webhook for a subscription's FIRST paid invoice whose checkout campaign (`meta_attribution.campaign_*`) is at most 14 days old, counted only while the invoice stays paid (`purchase_attribution_is_paid` — refunds and chargebacks drop out), and the write throws on error so the provider retries. Each event's CTA carries `utm_campaign=<slug>`; the middleware also keeps the last campaign of ANY link in `medchina-campanha` (14 days, httpOnly), which the checkout uses when its own link carries none (the `/planos` fallback, a return days later); with neither, the checkout clears the stored campaign. Pinned by `packages/db/tests/0042_leads.test.sql` and `0043_live_events_crud.test.sql`.
- **The public congress deck — `/palestra/publica`**: the same slides as the stage, rendered by the same `SlideRenderer`, but the SERVER page strips every speaker-only field (`script`, `stageNote`, `media.productionNote`) and drops the annex and two stage-only slides before anything reaches the client; `components/presentation/public-deck.tsx` receives slides as props and never imports `slides-deck.ts` (a client import of the list would ship the teleprompter to every visitor). The stage deck assumes a ≥ 1280 px projector; the public one centers its canvas by position (`.deck--public`), because on a phone the stage grid parked the scaled slide off-screen.
- Display typography: `font-display text-display-{2xl,xl,lg,md}` (fluid clamp scale from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/marketing.css`).
- Motion: GSAP only inside marketing client components via `<Reveal>`/`useGSAP` (transforms + `autoAlpha`, honors `prefers-reduced-motion`); never in admin code.
- Public pricing reads plans through `@flyee/billing/public` (`listPublicPlans`, service-role, read-only) with i18n placeholder fallback; the contact form sends via `@flyee/email` (`CONTACT_FORM_TO`) with a graceful not-configured hint.

## Clinical core (the MVP product)

- Routes: `/inicio` (app home — `DEFAULTS.appRoot`), `/pacientes` (+ `/novo`, `/[id]`), `/consultas/[id]`, `/onboarding` (the preparation of the practice — see Activation below), `/primeiros-passos` (the hub). Schema + RLS + guards: `packages/db/migrations/0020_clinical.sql` (`patients`, `consultations`, `anamnesis_answers`, `consultation_addenda`; row versioning enabled on all three clinical tables).
- **Absence is never a negative answer** (PRD §10.5): an anamnesis field with no value has NO row — clearing a field DELETES its answer. Never store an empty string or a "no".
- **A finalized consultation is frozen** (PRD §8.5): DB triggers reject any edit to the record or its answers; corrections go to `consultation_addenda` (append-only — no update/delete policy). The UI disables the fields and offers "Adicionar adendo".
- **The consultation is ONE page with a rail, never a wizard** (`components/product/consultation-step-rail.tsx` + `lib/consultation-rail.ts`): the journey already derives seven steps and their state, so the rail renders them and scrolls this page — nothing mounts, unmounts or gets disabled. Two reasons it may never become a step-at-a-time flow: the recorder unmounting stops the microphone tracks (measured, ~1s lost), and she writes WHILE recording, which is a spatial arrangement and not a sequence. A blocked step stays clickable because the place of the block is the place of the fix, and the server reason stays under the control. No "step N of M": the visible list grows and shrinks at runtime. Jump targets are an EXPLICIT map (`RAIL_TARGETS`) — a step with no place would scroll nowhere, which is what the two recording states of "next action" used to do. The screen is also measured now (`consultation.opened`, `consultation.step_jump`, `consultation.next_action`, migration `0104`; the event name is validated BOTH in the RPC and by a table check).
- Anamnesis blocks/fields are declared in `src/lib/anamnesis.ts` — the keys are STABLE (they are what the AI pipeline will map extracted values onto); tongue/pulse/palpation are professional observations (`source = professional_voice`), never inferred from patient speech (PRD §10.3). Two per-catalog switches replace hardcoded names: `alwaysReview` on a field forces every extracted value back for review (medications, tobacco, alcohol, substances, obstetric history, libido), and `when` on a block makes it CONDITIONAL. The one conditional block today is `gyneco` ("Ciclo menstrual e fertilidade", migration `0103_fertility_care.sql`): it applies when the practice declares the area (`profiles.practice_areas` ∋ `fertility`, edited in Settings via `update_practice_areas`) AND the patient is marked (`patients.fertility_care`). ONE function answers that — `fertility_care_applies(org, patient)` — for the screen (through `get_consultation_context` → `patient.fertilityCare`) and for the recording pipeline (service role), so the extraction never writes into a block she cannot see. Always go through `anamnesisBlocksFor(applicability, answeredKeys)` for RENDERING and PROMPTING and `countedAnamnesisBlocks(...)` for COUNTING, never `ANAMNESIS_BLOCKS` directly: the first keeps a block that no longer applies visible while it holds answers, the second is the "X de Y campos" total and the absence list the hypotheses prompt is given. The chief complaint is multi-line; prompts use `complaintOnOneLine` and retrieval/inline listings use `complaintTitle` (`lib/chief-complaint.ts`) — the first line is the case's title.
- **The pulse is read by POSITION** (her correction from real use, 2026-10-17): every item of the pulse — profundidade, ritmo, força, qualidade — belongs to an organ, so the `pulse` block holds TWELVE fields (`pulse.heart`, `pulse.small-intestine`, … `pulse.triple-burner`; organ alone, no cun/guan/chi — which finger feels what is her hand's knowledge) and the old one-line `tcm.pulse` is `retired: true`: it is never offered to her or to the extraction again, and survives only on the consultations that already hold one, editable (hiding it would read as "não informado" about a pulse that was informed). Three switches carry it, all declared in the catalog and never hardcoded by name: `retired` on a field, `optional` on a block (on screen for everyone, folded, and part of the total/absence list only once it holds an answer — otherwise every chart would read twelve fields short), and `vocabularyOnDemand` on a block (its fields share one vocabulary, so the chips are offered under the position she is writing in; four groups under twelve fields is some 240 chips). A pulse is "recorded" for the journey, the essential-exam limitation (`clinical-reasoning.ts`) and the library retrieval when ANY position has a value; the retrieval searches by organ in pt-BR (`PULSE_POSITION_ORGANS`), because `pulse.heart` embeds badly against a Portuguese corpus. The extraction may fill a position only when she named that organ out loud, and a pulse dictated with NO position must never be spread across the twelve — it comes back as a gap question quoting her words.
- **The MTC vocabulary chips COMPOSE her text, they never own it** (`src/lib/tcm-vocabulary.ts`, offered on tongue, palpation and each pulse position): a term that stands as its own item is the shape a chip writes, so the chip may take it back; a term inside a sentence SHE wrote ("pulso do coração fraco") lights the chip up — the finding IS on the chart — but tapping it takes her to the word instead of cutting it out. That was a real data loss: the chip matched her prose, removed the word and the autosave persisted it. `termPresence` is the rule (`absent` | `item` | `phrase`) and `toggleTerm` returns the value UNCHANGED for `phrase`.
- Activation (`src/lib/onboarding.ts`): steps use live predicates over real state; the aha moment is the first FINALIZED manual consultation. `OnboardingChecklistCard` on the home reads those facts.
- **The onboarding is the preparation of the practice, never a guided consultation** (revised 2026-10-12, after a user test in which the professional got lost when the guide asked her to start a consultation with no patient in the room). `/onboarding` is four steps, none of which needs a patient (`PREP_STEP_KEYS`): **`scope`** — how she works: modalities and areas, saved in ONE write by `complete_practice_scope` (migration `0119`). It also confirms the practice timezone WITHOUT a field: `proposeTimezone` (`lib/practice-context.ts`) adopts the browser's zone in silence when it keeps the same clock as the stored one (sampled today and half a year out, so "same offset this month" is not mistaken for "same clock") and asks only when the clocks differ — as "what time is it at your practice?", with two clocks to pick from. The RPC records which happened (`timezoneSource`: `browser | default | chosen | kept`), so a silent confirmation is never anonymous in the audit trail, and stamps `timezone_confirmed_at` once. **`signature`** — title and registration with a live `SignaturePreview` fed by the same `credentialLines()` the PDF renderers use. **`recording`** — `MicCheck` (asks the browser permission and shows the level; records and uploads NOTHING), the phone capture, and the two consent terms shown READ-ONLY from `consent_terms`: no acceptance is ever registered without a patient, because `consent_acceptances` is auditable and never deleted. **`next`** — book the next appointment, with the Pro-trial notice BEFORE the button (booking is an operational action, 0084). Rules that are load-bearing: only `scope` changes what the product does and it is a LIVE predicate (`hasPracticeContext`) no stored flag can stand in for; the other three leave nothing to observe, so "agora não" is remembered (`prep-*` in `onboarding_state.completed_steps`) and not asked again; each step says what the answer changed before she leaves it; and the flow ends on a summary of her own answers plus where the first consultation happens — never on "tudo pronto" over an empty home. Three surfaces read the SAME builders and cannot disagree about what is done: the flow, the home checklist (`buildOnboardingSteps`) and the hub (`buildPreparationSteps` + `buildFirstConsultationSteps`; recording is three extra rows for whoever records, not a separate track). The first consultation is guided where it happens — `FirstConsultationGuide` on `/consultas/[id]`, shown until the practice closes its first record or she dismisses it (`hooks/use-first-consultation-guide.ts`) and deliberately NOT numbered, because the screen numbers its own steps. "Fazer depois" stamps the `welcome` step, which is what stops `resolvePostAuthDestination` from sending her back at every sign-in (skipping used to record nothing). `/onboarding/guia` redirects. The flow is measured per step — `onboarding.step_viewed | step_completed | step_skipped | exited | completed` with a `prep_step` property (migration `0120`; closing the tab has no event and needs none: it is a `step_viewed` nothing closed). Pinned by `src/lib/onboarding-preparation.test.ts`, `src/lib/practice-context.test.ts` and `packages/db/tests/0048_onboarding_preparation_events.test.sql`.
- **Modalities beyond the five** (migration `0119_practice_modalities_other.sql`): `profiles.practice_modalities_other` holds what she typed, in its OWN column, apart from the closed list. It has NO clinical effect — it never widens the therapeutic plan, never ranks a library document and is **never sent to a model**: a label is 60 characters of her own words, which is room for an instruction, and the assistants carry clinical-safety rules that must not be reachable from a settings field. It exists so a professional whose practice is not on the list still sees herself here, and so the team can see who is using the platform — the account dossier shows it ("Outras modalidades") and `/admin/insights` can count it. `PracticeModalitiesField` edits both lists in one control (used by the preparation and by Settings); a typed label that names a known modality becomes the known one, so the free path can never declare something the product would then ignore. The rules live in SQL — `practice_modalities_other_valid` is also the column's CHECK, because `profiles` is writable by its owner through PostgREST: at most 10 labels of 2–60 characters, no control characters, no case-insensitive repeats, and never starting with `= + - @`, the characters a spreadsheet reads as a formula (this list will be exported by whoever studies it). The audit records the COUNT, never the labels. Pinned by `packages/db/tests/0047_practice_modalities_other.test.sql` (25 assertions, including the write around the RPC that the row guard must refuse).
- **Consent gates CAPTURE, not reasoning** (migrations `0022_consent_recordings.sql` and `0102_ai_record_notice.sql`, PRD §9.5): three patient authorizations (`audio-recording`, `ai-processing`, `clinical-images`) plus one CIÊNCIA (`ai-record-notice`) are seeded as versioned `consent_terms`; the patient screen `/pacientes/[id]/consentimentos` records each (revoking stamps `revoked_at`, never deletes — auditable). `has_active_consent(org, patient, slug)` is the shared answer, and a DB trigger REJECTS inserting a `recordings` row without an active `audio-recording` consent. **The line to hold**: an active `ai-processing` consent is required by what COLLECTS or exposes new data — transcribing audio, analysing an attached image, the MCP connector — and NOT by reasoning over what the professional typed (hypotheses, plan, AI summary, case review). Those ask one thing instead: that the patient has not said no, via `patient_refused_ai_reasoning(org, patient)` (a revoked acceptance, or `decision = false` on her own device — never having been asked is not a refusal; error code `ai_consent_refused`). The ciência is evidence she was told her record may be organized with AI support: it authorizes nothing, blocks nothing, and is never chased with an alert. Refusing to record never blocks manual care. **A consent term has ONE text, in pt-BR** — `consent_terms` has no locale column, and `/consentir` opens on the patient’s phone, which carries no locale cookie. That is why `patient_consent_sessions.presented_locale` stays fenced to the five locales that predate zh-CN: it is EVIDENCE of the language the term appeared in, not a preference, and nothing writes it (it sits at its `pt-BR` default). Adding a locale to that CHECK before translating the term would only make it possible to record that a term was shown in a language no term exists in. It moves when the terms do.
- **Web recording** (`components/product/consultation-recorder.tsx`, PRD §4.1/§12.4): MediaRecorder capture in the consultation sidebar (while not finalized). Audio goes to the private `transcriptions` bucket under `<org_id>/<recording_id>.webm`; the `recordings` row flips to `uploaded` ONLY after storage confirms — nothing claims to be "sent" before the server accepts it. The bucket + path convention are shared with `@flyee/transcribe` (0007), which is where the AI pipeline picks up next.
- **Capture UX invariants** (learned from a real session that lost a consultation — treat these as load-bearing, not polish): **(1) the microphone is opened BEFORE any server state exists.** The old order created the `recordings` row first, so a refused permission left an open row that made every later capture fail `recording_already_open` — a consultation permanently unable to record. No device, no row. **(2) An open row is never a dead end**: on mount, a row in `recording`/`local`/`uploading` with no locally persisted audio is surfaced as an orphan with a "discard and unblock" action (`recordings-panel` also allows discard from any stuck status, with a confirmation that names the different consequence). **(3) The recorder never silently disappears** — when another tab holds the session the page renders a "record in this tab" card over `takeOver()`, because it is the ONLY capture surface. **(4) Capture state follows her down the page** (fixed bar with dot + mm:ss + level + pause/finish): the sidebar card scrolls away during a 50-minute session. **(5) Elapsed time comes from the wall clock**, never accumulated `setInterval` ticks, which a background tab throttles. **(6) A level meter is the only honest proof** that sound is arriving, plus a 60s silence watchdog. **(7) Losing the device is detected** (`track.onended`/`onmute`) and alerted OUT of the tab via `lib/capture-alert.ts` — tab title + a **silent** Web Notification (there is a patient in the room: no audible cue, and a beep would be captured into the audio being transcribed); notification permission is requested only AFTER a first successful capture. **(8) While a capture is in flight the anamnesis subtitle states the contract** — the AI drafts for review and never overwrites what she typed — because that guarantee was enforced in code and invisible in the UI.
- **Immutability guards protect content, not housekeeping** (migration `0021`): the finalized-consultation triggers skip nested/cascade operations (`pg_trigger_depth() > 1`) and only reject changes to the CLINICAL payload — so account/patient deletion (LGPD erasure, PRD §14.5) cascades through a finalized record, while a professional still cannot rewrite it from the app.
- **Therapeutic plan — Pro** (migration `0026_therapeutic_plan.sql`, PRD §10.9/§10.10; `lib/therapeutic-plan.ts`, `POST /api/consultations/[id]/plan`, `components/product/plan-panel.tsx`): a per-modality DRAFT (acupuncture, Chinese dietary therapy, moxibustion, auriculotherapy, cupping) built on the hypotheses she ACCEPTED/edited — the plan follows her clinical direction, it does not re-diagnose. On demand and Pro-gated like the hypotheses. **Safety is enforced in code, not the prompt**: sensitive factors (medications, pregnancy, anticoagulants, pacemaker, surgery, lesions, allergies) are DERIVED from the recorded anamnesis by `lib/clinical-safety.ts` (`detectSafetyFlags`, categorized; `SENSITIVE` is the same union the anamnesis extraction uses) and stored on the plan — a fluent draft cannot hide them; moxibustion never ships without its pre-application contraindication checklist (seeded from the flags if the model drops it); citations are dropped unless they resolve to a retrieved chunk. A plan is a `draft` until the professional **validates** it (must acknowledge the surfaced contraindications first) — validating stamps `validated_by/at`; editing any field returns it to draft (a validation was of a specific plan). Every field editable (PRD §10.9 "sempre editável"). Model + prompt_version recorded (§10.10); frozen with the consultation (§8.5); row-versioned; one plan per consultation.
- **Issuing the plan as a signed document** (PRD §9.8; `lib/plan-document.tsx`, `POST /api/consultations/[id]/plan/issue`): a VALIDATED plan (only — a draft is refused with `plan_not_validated`) becomes a QR-verifiable PDF through `@flyee/documents` (`issueDocument` stores it in the private `documents` bucket, records the sha256 and a 12-char `verify_code`; the public page is `/verify/[code]`). The PDF is a **snapshot** — it renders what was validated, independent of later edits. Reissuing bumps the version, links `parent_id` and **revokes** the previous one (still verifiable, flagged as superseded). Rendering uses `@react-pdf/renderer` (in `serverExternalPackages`, standard Helvetica — no external font, self-contained on serverless). Two non-obvious constraints, both learned the hard way: `plan-document.tsx` must **NOT** be `server-only` (that marker forces the `react-server` condition, which resolves React to the RSC build and breaks @react-pdf's reconciler), and it imports `React` explicitly (JSX compiles with the classic runtime outside the Next/SWC pipeline). Labels are resolved by the route via `getTranslations` and passed in, so the renderer stays i18n-clean. Modality descriptors live once in `lib/plan-modalities.ts`, shared by the panel, the route and the PDF.
- **Clinical reasoning — Pro** (migration `0025_clinical_reasoning.sql`, PRD §10.8; `lib/clinical-reasoning.ts`, `POST /api/consultations/[id]/hypotheses`, `components/product/hypotheses-panel.tsx`): disharmony-pattern hypotheses over the recorded anamnesis, retrieving from the clinical library (`packages/knowledge` RAG, three global collections kept classified by KIND — traditional / internal protocol / scientific evidence, PRD §9.9). Prepared **on demand**, NOT in the recording pipeline: a pattern is read from tongue and pulse, which are the professional's own observations (never inferred from the recording, PRD §10.3), so reasoning at transcription time would always be under-determined. Rules enforced in CODE, not the prompt: strength is **correspondence with the recorded data** (weak/moderate/strong), never confidence/probability (PRD §10.8); a citation is dropped unless it resolves to a chunk actually retrieved (an invented source manufactures authority); missing tongue/pulse forces a `limitation` and caps correspondence below "strong"; `contradicting_signs`/`missing_data` are first-class. Each row records `model` + `prompt_version` (PRD §10.10). The heading (§10.8) and disclaimer (§10.11) are the PRD's verbatim text; nothing is red (a hypothesis is not a risk). She accepts / **edits** (flips to her reading) / rejects with a note (PRD §10.10); re-preparing replaces only `draft` rows, never her decisions. Frozen with the consultation (§8.5) and row-versioned. Gated on the Pro entitlement via the same `org_audio_allowance` (`clinical_reasoning`): the trial IS Pro; Assistente has minutes but not reasoning; suspended/exhausted gets nothing.
- **Trial + minutes** (migration `0024_trial_minutes.sql`, PRD §5.7/§5.8): audio minutes are the billable unit; `org_audio_allowance(org)` is the SINGLE answer to "may this workspace use AI, and how much is left?" — computed in SQL so the app (`lib/usage.ts`, `hooks/use-audio-allowance.ts`) and the DB guard can never disagree. **The limit is checked only when something STARTS**: a DB trigger rejects inserting a `recordings` row without allowance, which is exactly why `processRecording` does NOT re-check it — the row's existence IS the authorization, so an already-captured consultation is never stranded (PRD §5.8 forbids interrupting a recording in flight; it overruns, warns, and the NEXT one is refused). The Pro trial starts via `start_pro_trial(org, via)` at the first OPERATIONAL action of any kind — the recorder's deliberate confirmation, but equally saving an appointment, committing an import or using the library (migration `0084`; `lib/pro-trial.ts` fires it after the action's own success, never blocking it). Browsing still starts nothing, and the origin is kept in `pro_trials.started_via` because "what starts trials" became a real commercial question. Two consequences to honor: the RPC reports `trial_started` so only a REAL insert fires the StartTrial conversion and the e-mail drip, and any screen that may start one must SAY it started — user-facing copy that promises "only at the first AI consultation" is now false. It ends on days OR minutes, and when it ends the chart stays fully readable — only new capture/processing stops. A paid audio plan never falls back to the trial pool (that would defeat the superadmin kill-switch). Consumption is measured SERVER-side (`billableSeconds`: the transcript's last timestamp is the floor, so a browser cannot under-report its bill) and recorded ONLY on success — a failed transcription bills nothing. Usage is an append-only ledger writable by the service role alone. Trial days/minutes and plan prices/limits are configurable rows (`platform_settings` 'trial' key, `plans.limits.audio_minutes`), never constants. Alerts at 80/95/100% are idempotent via `usage_alerts` unique (org, window, threshold).
- **Dunning grace + named causes** (migration `0054_billing_grace_period.sql`): `past_due` used to cut every AI capability the instant the provider reported a failed charge — mid-appointment. It now keeps the plan usable for a configurable window (`platform_settings` 'dunning' key, default 7 days) counted from `subscriptions.past_due_since`, which the webhook stamps on failure and clears on recovery; `billing_past_due_grace_ends()` is the ONE answer all three gates share (`org_audio_allowance`, `org_message_allowance`, `org_entitlements`) so they cannot disagree about the same workspace. The allowance also gained `reason` (`ok | past_due_grace | past_due_blocked | suspended | pack_only | trial_not_started | trial_over | cycle_exhausted | no_plan`): screens used to INFER why they were blocked from `canStart`/`trialAvailable`, which is how "your minutes ran out" got shown to someone whose card had failed. Branch on `reason`, never on the flags — a recused card is not fixed by buying anything, and a suspension is not fixed by the professional at all. Suspension is now absolute (it no longer survives on leftover trial days).
- **À-la-carte minutes** (migration `0055_audio_minute_packs.sql`, PRD §5.8): a second pool (`audio_minute_packs`) consumed only AFTER the cycle pool, sold as one-off `plans` rows marked `is_addon` (excluded from both pricing grids) through `startPackCheckout` + `complete_pack_checkout_billing_operation` — a separate path because the subscription completion always writes a `subscriptions` row and an org may hold only one live subscription. Granted by the webhook on the PAID invoice (idempotent on `invoice_key`), never at checkout start. **Consumption is attributed at WRITE time** (`audio_usage.cycle_seconds`/`pack_seconds`, summing to `seconds`): deriving pack usage from "overflow past the cycle limit" silently refunds the pack at every cycle turnover, because the overflow resets with the window while the purchase does not. `apply_recording_result` claims the usage row BEFORE debiting any pack — the unique index from 0030 is the fence, so a lost retry race cannot spend the pack twice. Purchased minutes survive `past_due`, cancellation and a downgrade (the money is already ours) but never `admin_suspended`. Only paid plans with minutes may buy (`pack_purchasable`, enforced again in the server action) so a pack tops up a subscription instead of replacing one. A pack purchase clears the window's `usage_alerts` rows — buying changes the denominator, and without the reset the 80/95/100% warnings would never fire again that cycle. Support grants go through `grant_audio_minute_pack()` (superadmin-only, audited), because `audio_usage.seconds` is checked `> 0` and cannot credit anything back.
- **Comped plans** (migration `0067_admin_plan_assignment.sql`, `/admin/billing` → Subscriptions): `set_org_plan(org, plan, note)` puts a workspace on a tier with no checkout — betas, partners, the team's own workspace. RLS always allowed the raw write (`subscriptions_all_superadmin` is `for all`), which is exactly why this exists: doing it by hand walks past five traps. **The period bounds must stay NULL** — `org_audio_allowance` counts usage inside the current period and a comped plan has no provider cycle to advance `current_period_end`, so a fixed end date silently stops metering entirely (measured: 5.000 minutes consumed under an elapsed period reported as 0 used, `can_start = true`); with NULL bounds the allowance falls back to the self-renewing calendar month. The others: UPDATE not INSERT (`subscriptions_org_live_unique` allows one live row), `subscriptions.period` must follow the plan, "remove the plan" means assigning the FREE one (no live subscription ⇒ `org_entitlements` reports `active: false` and the library 402s), and a raw write leaves no audit trail. A provider-backed subscription is REFUSED (`provider_managed`): changing the tier locally while Stripe/Asaas keeps charging the old one is a billing inconsistency no console should create by accident. Self-assignment is deliberately allowed — a superadmin already holds every privilege, so forbidding it would be theatre — but the audit event stamps `self_grant`, which is the case an auditor looks for.
- **AI pipeline** (PRD §10.2; `lib/clinical-pipeline.ts` + `lib/clinical-extraction.ts`, job `lib/clinical-jobs.ts` on event `medchina/recording.process`, kicked off by `POST /api/recordings/[id]/process` with the template's queue-or-inline fallback): an `uploaded` recording → diarized transcript (`@flyee/transcribe` + Gemini) → DRAFT anamnesis. The extraction rules are enforced in code AND prompt, not the prompt alone: absence is never written as a negative (no row); tongue/pulse/palpation only fill from a practitioner-dictated line (`source = professional_voice`), never inferred from patient speech (a violation is DROPPED, not trusted); **WHO SPOKE is decided by the diarization, for every field** (`resolveAnswerOrigin`) — the model's own `source` label was written to the chart unchecked outside those four fields, so a sentence the PROFESSIONAL said could be stored and shown as "relato da paciente" and then reach the hypotheses prompt as the patient's words (reported from a real online consultation); when the quote has no anchor or the practitioner's speaker is unknown — a teleconsultation where the patient's voice never reaches the microphone has ONE speaker — nothing is asserted: `provenance.originVerified = false`, the value comes back as `attention`, the chip reads "Origem não confirmada" and the reasoning prompt says the same; every value carries provenance (transcript quote + timestamp) for review; gaps land in `consultations.ai_gaps` as questions, never answers. The consultation moves to `awaiting_review`; a value the professional already typed by hand is never overwritten. Gated on a SEPARATE `ai-processing` consent (recording consent alone is not enough). GEMINI_API_KEY is server-only — processing is a server route/job, never a client call. Editing an AI-filled field flips it to `source = professional, state = edited` so a human decision is never mistaken for AI output.

## Clinical library — the out-of-consultation layer

The product's second loop: the platform is useful BETWEEN consultations, not only during them. Five phases, all verified end-to-end; commercial rationale and the licensing review live in `docs/LICENSING-LIBRARY.md`.

- **Library chat with citations** (migrations `0042`/`0043`, `/biblioteca`): a study assistant (seeded assistant `biblioteca-mtc`, Gemini) grounded in the MTC collections through the existing `packages/knowledge` RAG. `POST /api/ai/chat` gained: a **data-driven monthly quota** (`assistants.config.quota_limit_key` names a `plans.limits` key — absent key = unlimited; the SQL RPC `org_message_allowance` is the single answer, the UI only displays it), the retrieved **sources returned to the client** as a sentinel-framed JSON prelude (`SOURCES_SENTINEL`, opt-in via `includeSources`) and persisted in `messages.metadata` so a reopened conversation keeps its citations. Consumption warns at 80/95/100% through the same bell mechanism as audio minutes (`alertAfterLibraryMessage`, `usage_alerts.meter`).
- **Case review — Pro** (migration `0044`, same chat): a conversation may be ABOUT one patient (`conversations.patient_id`, `on delete cascade` — LGPD erasure takes the conversations that carry her clinical data). Gate enforced in code, never only in the UI: the Pro entitlement (`clinicalReasoning`). Deliberately NOT gated on `ai-processing` consent — that term authorizes CAPTURING the consultation (recording her voice, sending audio out to transcribe), while case review rereads a record the professional already wrote; requiring it locked migrated patients out of the feature with nothing to fix in the room. RLS and the audit trail are the boundaries that apply. The record is loaded by `lib/patient-case.ts` and injected with rules (chart data is never citable as `[n]`, absence is never negation, never conclude or prescribe). On an existing conversation the STORED `patient_id` is the authority — a client cannot reassign it. Every use is audited (`library.case_review`).
- **Pre-consultation briefing** (`components/product/consultation-briefing-dialog.tsx` + `lib/patient-briefing.ts`, entry points in the agenda and the home): alerts, last consultation, accepted patterns, validated plan and pending drafts/gaps — assembled **deterministically** from the record. No AI call, so no consent gate, no cost, every plan; the AI conversation stays one click away for Pro.
- **Browsable acervo** (migration `0045`, `/biblioteca/acervo`): the 459 seeded cards, searchable by name/code/pinyin with facets by kind and meridian. Safeguards from the licensing review are load-bearing: authenticated-only, visible attribution, `knowledge_collections.browsable` as a kill-switch (product control, NOT security — RLS already allows authenticated reads), purpose notice. Chat citations link to their acervo page (`KnowledgeSourceRef.documentId`).
- **Her own protocols** (migration `0047`, `/biblioteca/protocolos`): the professional writes her protocols into an org-scoped `meus-protocolos` collection (created on demand). No new table or policy — a collection slug is unique PER ORG, so `resolveCollectionIds` under her RLS resolves HER collection and never another's. Saving indexes through the same queue-or-inline path as the admin console; her protocol then comes back cited as "Protocolo interno" in the chat, the hypotheses and the plan.
- **Telemetry**: the layer emits `library.message_sent` (with `has_patient`), `library.quota_hit`, `case_review.started`, `acervo.document_opened`, `citation.opened`, `briefing.opened` and `protocol.saved`. Adding an event means extending BOTH allowlists in `product_events` (name check + the RPC's property allowlist, migration `0048`) — that boundary is what keeps clinical content and UUIDs out of the operational table. Note `trackProductEvent` must terminate the PostgREST builder (`.then()`): a bare `void supabase.rpc(...)` never issues the request.
- **Morning briefing** (`lib/agenda-jobs.ts`, Inngest cron): one bell notification per workspace on days that actually have appointments, idempotent per local day.

## Platform admin & account

- Superadmin area at `src/app/(dashboard)/admin`: `layout.tsx` is a server gate on `profiles.is_superadmin` (RLS remains the real defense); the Admin menu group renders only for superadmins (`hooks/use-is-superadmin.ts`). Consoles: `/admin` (metrics via `admin_metrics()`), `/admin/organizations` (tenants + users; ban/unban, 2FA state and 2FA reset need `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`), `/admin/billing`, `/admin/ai`, `/admin/knowledge`, `/admin/audit` (audit_events + access_events + wa_messages), `/admin/insights`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/announcements`, `/admin/help`, `/admin/blog`, `/admin/eventos`, `/admin/leads`. **Admin console copy is hardcoded pt-BR, deliberately outside i18n** (revised 2026-09-19): the operator surface has exactly ONE reader, the platform owner, so routing it through six catalogs buys nothing and slows every edit — the same reasoning the funnel pages already use. Write new admin strings directly in Portuguese; keep code comments in English like the rest of the repo, and never translate a value that comes from the database (enum, slug, status) — map it to a label instead, the way `STATUS_LABEL`/`FLAG_LABEL`/`MINUTE_REASON` do in the accounts console. Everything user-facing stays i18n. The grid chrome around that copy is not yours to translate: `components/data-grid/data-table.tsx` reads search/columns/filters/export and the pagination label out of MUI X's own locale pack for the active locale, so it follows the app language in every console (pass `labels` only when a page wants different wording).

- **Granting the superadmin role** (migration `0096_superadmin_grant.sql`, `/admin/organizations` → the user's kebab): the flag itself is FENCED by a trigger on `profiles`, because `profiles_update_own` (0000) plus the legacy column grants meant one `PATCH /rest/v1/profiles?id=eq.<self>` with `{"is_superadmin": true}` promoted any signed-in user to platform operator — read access to every patient record in the database. The fence keys on WHO is asking (`is_superadmin()` reads the database; PostgREST cannot forge it), never on a transaction-local flag the caller could set itself. The console's write is `set_user_superadmin(user, value, note)` — a definer RPC, needed because RLS gives even a superadmin no update policy on somebody else's profile, and audited as `admin.user.superadmin_granted`/`_revoked` with no `org_id` (a platform-level act). Self-change is refused in BOTH directions: granting to yourself is the escalation the fence exists to stop, and self-demotion would let the last operator lock the platform out of `/admin` with one click — which is also why the RPC needs no "last superadmin" case (the actor is always a superadmin who stays one). A session with no JWT (service role, migration, psql) is still allowed through: that is the 0001 bootstrap that makes the FIRST superadmin, and the only way back if the set is ever emptied. Behaviour is pinned by `packages/db/tests/0029_superadmin_grant.test.sql`.

- **Account management view** (migration `0104_admin_accounts_overview.sql`, `/admin/organizations` → Accounts tab): the console used to list workspace name, plan name and member count, which answers none of the operator's real questions. `admin_accounts_overview()` answers them in ONE superadmin-gated query per load: who the account is (owner name, e-mail, phone, professional title and registration — the workspace name is free text the professional typed at sign-up and is frequently just "Consultório", so it identifies nothing), the live plan and days to renewal, the Pro trial's days and minute ceiling, the minute pool, 30-day use (records, recordings, minutes, library) with days-since-last-activity, sign-up attribution, and per-account flags. Minutes, trial and entitlement are READ from `org_audio_allowance` rather than recalculated, so the console cannot drift from what the product enforces; `renewalDays` stays NULL for a comped plan (0067 leaves the period bounds NULL on purpose) and the UI says "comped" instead of inventing a date. The summary tiles are filters and their counts come from the same query as the rows, so the two can never disagree. It also adds up the money: `mrrCents` is what the PROVIDERS charge each month (yearly plans normalized to a twelfth), `atRiskMrrCents` is what is overdue or scheduled to cancel, and `compedMrrCents` is what the console gave away — a comped plan (0067) has no provider behind it, so counting it as revenue would be lying to ourselves. Behaviour is pinned by `packages/db/tests/0037_admin_accounts_overview.test.sql` (including MRR ≠ comped); the screen itself was walked against a seeded local database (tiles, revenue band, rows, detail dialog, filters, deep link) before shipping.

- **Our own accounts are not customers** (migration `0118_staff_org_entitlements.sql`): granting the superadmin role handed someone the whole platform and left THEIR workspace on the free tier — a brand-new operator account was still refused the 201st row of an import, because `plans.limits.import_rows` says 200 (0076). The database already named the idea: the dossier (0106) reports `staffAccount` — "any member of this workspace is a superadmin" — to keep the conversion arithmetic honest. 0118 promotes that observation to a rule the four entitlement gates obey (`org_import_allowance`, `org_audio_allowance`, `org_message_allowance`, `org_entitlements`), through `is_staff_org(org)` and `staff_plan()`. Three things it deliberately does NOT do: it does not grant infinity — a staff workspace inherits the catalog's **most capable active monthly plan** (ordered by audio minutes, then price), so it is unlimited exactly where that tier is unlimited (imports carry no `import_rows` key) and metered where it is metered, and nothing here invents a number or lets an operator account run an unbounded provider bill; it does not override a plan that is actually being charged (a staff workspace holding a real paid subscription keeps it — otherwise the platform would bill one tier and meter another); and it never outranks the kill switch (every branch sits behind `admin_suspended`, the one control that may have no exception). It is a property of the WORKSPACE, not of who is asking, so an operator reading a customer's allowance still sees the customer's own. The grant dialog states all of it before the click, and the revoke copy says the workspace drops back to the plan it really has. Pinned by `packages/db/tests/0046_staff_org_entitlements.test.sql` — 24 assertions, including the customer beside the operator who must not move, the staff workspace that pays and keeps its plan, and suspension winning over every branch.

- **Account dossier** (migration `0106_account_dossier.sql`, Accounts tab → row kebab → Account detail, types and the verdict in `components/account-dossier.ts`): everything the platform knows about ONE account — registration, money, use, failures, the AI's report card, consent and access — in one query for one workspace, fired when the dialog opens so the list query (0104) stays cheap. Four sections are always visible (who she is / money / is she using it / anything broken) and the rest waits behind one disclosure; the top line is a derived verdict — the single thing standing in the account's way and what to do about it, first match wins, ordered by what an operator does first (something we broke → money stuck → a door she cannot open → the clock). What the field list encodes, each learned from the schema rather than guessed: a failed recording burns NO minutes (`apply_recording_result` writes usage only on success), so a broken account reads as a LIGHT account everywhere else and failures need their own section that says "nothing broken" affirmatively; lifetime revenue is net because `revert_paid_invoice` flips a row to 'refunded' instead of inserting a negative, so the refunded total sits beside it; `ai_answer_decisions` has no 'accepted' row (0059), so acceptance is what still stands, never a rate from that table; `access_events` counts SESSIONS and includes support visits, so sign-ins filter `impersonated_by is null` and an empty table reads "no trail"; a comped plan has no invoice and no provider ids ("never charged", not a dash); an abandoned checkout ('incomplete', with a live payment link) is invisible to 0104's live-subscription filter and surfaces only here; and three date fields are clamped at zero because imported charts and migrated payments predate the workspace — `greatest(null, 0)` is 0 in Postgres, which would have claimed instant activation for an account that never activated. Privacy is structural: no patient name, no clinical text, no consent free text, no deletion-request reason, no `audit_events.metadata` (it carries patient ids), no unsubscribe token, and the fiscal id only as a type plus two digits. Pinned by `packages/db/tests/0039_account_dossier.test.sql` — 29 assertions over a worst-case fixture, including two that assert what must NOT appear in the payload.

- **What the AI costs, per account** (migrations `0115_ai_spend.sql` / `0116_accounts_overview_cost.sql` / `0117_account_dossier_spend.sql`; `src/lib/ai-spend.ts`, price book at `/admin/ai` → Custo dos modelos): the console could say how MUCH AI a workspace used — audio seconds, library units, counts of hypotheses — and nothing at all about what any of it cost, because **no provider usage was ever read**: `messages.tokens_in/tokens_out` existed since 0002 and nothing ever wrote them, and `ChatProvider` did not return usage at all. The interface now takes an optional `onUsage` sink (`ChatUsage`, reported by all four providers BEFORE the failure checks — a call cut at max_tokens or stopped by a safety filter was billed in full), and every place that spends provider money records one `ai_spend` row: transcription (`packages/transcribe`, one row per model call, so a fallback chain and its continuations are all counted, with the seconds only on the first — the continuations re-read the SAME audio), anamnesis, hypotheses, plan, attachment analysis, library chat, case review and the operator's own `/admin/insights` questions (`org_id` NULL: platform overhead, charged to no workspace). Embeddings are the one deliberate gap, documented where they live. **Prices are configuration, never code** — `platform_settings` key 'ai_prices', per million tokens in the provider's own currency, shipped EMPTY: an unpriced model produces `priced = false` and zero cost, and every console reports the unpriced COUNT beside the total, because a zero next to 400 unpriced calls is a missing price list and not a cheap month. Cost is stored in **USD micros** (millionths of a dollar — a 1.000-token call rounds to zero in cents) and converted only when the operator sets `usdToBrl`; with no rate the consoles show dollars and the margin stays empty instead of adding two currencies. Saving prices re-prices the whole ledger (`reprice_ai_spend`), which is what keeps the first month of measurement from being stuck at zero. 0115 also backfills transcription history from `audio_usage`'s real seconds, marked `estimated` — the seconds are measured, the model attribution is not, and the UI never lets an estimate read as a measured bill. The account list carries the 30-day cost per row (sortable), three FACT filters (it spent · it spent while paying us nothing · it spent more than it pays — never an invented "expensive" threshold), and a platform panel split by what the money bought; the dossier shows the headline cost and margin in the always-visible money section and the full breakdown — by feature with its tokens and audio seconds, by model, six months of history — behind the disclosure. Pinned by `packages/db/tests/0045_ai_spend.test.sql` (40 assertions, including the arithmetic that must not round a fractional call to zero and an unpriced call that must not read as free).

- **The workspace name is patient-facing** (`auth.practice*` in all six catalogs): sign-up asks for the practice NAME with an example, not "Consultório ou clínica" — the old label named a category and that is what people typed back, leaving workspaces called just "Consultório" (the admin console now identifies accounts by the professional, which is the other half of the fix). The hint says who sees it, and it is true: `organizations.name` reaches the patient as `practiceName` in the document-share e-mail and on the consent page.

- **Daily operator watch** (`src/lib/admin-jobs.ts`, cron 08:30 BRT, served with every other job at `/api/inngest`): the console answers "which account needs me today?" only for somebody who opens it, but a trial ends on its own schedule and an overdue payment waits for nobody. The job reads the SAME `admin_accounts_overview()` the screen renders — as the service role, which 0104 lets in explicitly because a cron has no session — and sends one bell notification plus one e-mail (`sendAdminAccountsDigestEmail`) to every superadmin, linking to `/admin/organizations?filter=<group>` so the alert lands on the accounts it names. Three rules keep it readable: nothing to report means no digest at all (an alert that arrives every morning stops being read), `trial_over` is only news for 48 hours (the flag itself stays true until she converts), and `notifications.source_key` (`admin-watch:<date>:<user>`) is the idempotency fence for the WHOLE digest — an operator who already has today's row gets no second e-mail, which is also why `notifyUsers` now reports `createdFor`. Pinned by `src/lib/admin-jobs.test.ts`.

- **Account deletion** (migration `0099_account_deletion.sql`, `/admin/organizations` → the user's kebab → `delete-account-dialog.tsx`, server action `deleteAccount`): permanent removal of a professional's account and everything it holds.
