Three traps make it more than "delete the user": **(1) the data is not on the user** — `organizations.created_by` is SET NULL, so deleting `auth.users` alone leaves the workspace and every chart alive with nobody able to see it; the unit is the account PLUS every workspace she is the only member of. **(2) The org cascade is not erasure** — `record_versions` has `org_id` but no FK, and the versioning trigger snapshots every row the cascade deletes, so the RPC purges that history explicitly. **(3) Files are outside the transaction** — `storage.objects` refuses SQL deletes, so they go through the Storage API after the commit, listed by `admin_orphaned_account_storage`, which REFUSES any workspace or person that still exists (it feeds a service-role delete and must never be able to point at a live practice) and is therefore safe to retry. Order in the action: re-read the preview → cancel any provider subscription at Stripe/Asaas and mark it canceled (a failure there deletes nothing; the RPC independently refuses `provider_subscription_live`) → `admin_delete_account(user, confirm_email, reason)` in ONE transaction → purge files. Inside that transaction the order is explicit (migration `0101_account_deletion_holds.sql`): rows that HOLD workspace data through NO ACTION/RESTRICT references — QR consent session items and capture authorizations, then consent acceptances, then issued documents — are deleted first, holder before held, because Postgres checks those references mid-cascade, in queue order, NOT after every sibling cascade has run (the first real deletion aborted on `patient_consent_session_items_acceptance_id_fkey`; the document RESTRICTs had only passed by an accident of FK creation order). The FKs themselves stay strict — they guard consent evidence and issued documents in normal operation. A catalog tripwire in the test fails as soon as a new NO ACTION/RESTRICT reference into deletable data appears, until the RPC clears it too. Refused in the database, not only in the dialog: yourself, any superadmin (demote first), the owner of a workspace other people belong to, support sessions; the typed e-mail and the reason are checked in SQL too. A plain member of someone else's clinic just leaves — her authorship detaches, the clinic keeps its records. What survives on purpose: the platform-level audit event `admin.account.deleted` (counts only — never a name or clinical text, since it outlives the data), anonymized `product_events`, and backups until retention prunes them. The patient-level flow stays a request marker (`patients.deletion_requested_at`, 0028); this is the only hard delete of clinical data in the product — and since migration `0105_workspace_deletion_guard.sql`, the only one that exists at all: the template's `organizations_delete_owner` policy is gone, because an owner's `DELETE /rest/v1/organizations` cascaded the clinical tables while leaving every `record_versions` snapshot and every stored file behind, audited nothing, and aborted half-way on any practice with issued documents or a QR consent session. A trigger (`guard_organization_delete`) stands behind the missing policy — a DELETE policy is one careless migration away from coming back — and lets through only a session with no JWT (service role, migration, psql) or a superadmin outside a support visit. Behaviour is pinned by `packages/db/tests/0032_account_deletion.test.sql` — a worst-case fixture (finalized consultation, issued document held by RESTRICT FKs, closed import, change history, files) plus catalog-wide scans for any leftover workspace row or person FK, so a table added later is covered without anyone remembering this test.
- **Live events and leads** (`/admin/eventos`, `/admin/leads`; migrations `0112`/`0113`). **`/admin/eventos`** is the events console: a list by situation (upcoming · live · ended · archived — `StatTile` filters over `live_events_overview()`; upcoming soonest first, the rest newest first, undated last), each card with its funnel — visits → registrations → attendance → purchases — as `MetricBars`; **new** events start as drafts and **duplicates** copy content and settings, never registrations, date, stream or recording (`duplicate_live_event`). `/admin/eventos/[id]` has five tabs: **Resultados** (`live_event_results`: a `MetricBars` chain registration → group → conversation → watched → 20 min+, device of the group click, registrations by channel with their visits, attributed sales), **Inscritas** (THIS event's 1:1 list: **"open conversation" one row at a time and never in bulk**, stamping `last_whatsapp_opened_at`), **Página** (the copy), **Configuração** (state, Brasília date, the Community owner's number as a `PhoneField` stored as `55` + 11 digits, invite, stream, recording, per-network limit, what the page does once ended, archive, delete) and **E-mails** (one button per reminder, each sending once per person — the per-kind column is the fence; queued through Inngest with an inline fallback). The LIFECYCLE is enforced in the database: the slug freezes once the event was EVER published (`published_at`, stamped once by the trigger and never cleared — moving it back to draft does not unlock it) or registered for, only a never-published empty draft can be deleted (`delete_live_event`: `not_draft` / `was_published` / `has_registrations`, audited with the reason), anything else is archived (a CHECK allows it only for drafts and ended events). `updated_by` is stamped by a trigger from the session; audit metadata never carries personal data. **`/admin/leads`** is the PEOPLE view — one row per person across events, read in pages past PostgREST's 1,000-row cap (`lib/fetch-all-pages.ts`; a `.limit()` above it drops rows silently), with an event picker that scopes the counters, the table and the export together: opt-out with a reason, LGPD erasure through `purge_lead`, and the ONLY export: the consented, not-opted-out audience, one line per person, in Meta's customer-list headers (`phone` as `55`+digits WITHOUT "+", which would trip the formula guard and ship an unmatchable `'+55…`; `email`, `fn`, `ln`, `country`), audited by count (the grids' generic export is OFF, `enableExport={false}`). The shared `DataTable` is the MIT grid (no column pinning), so row actions stay reachable on a laptop only because secondary columns start hidden (`initialColumnVisibility`).
- Every mutation records an audit event through `lib/audit.ts` (`recordAudit`) — keep that up when adding admin/tenant writes. Sign-ins are logged automatically by a DB trigger (migration 0016); users see their own in `/settings/security`.
- **Support impersonation** (migration `0057_impersonation.sql`, `lib/impersonation-actions.ts`, trigger in `/admin/organizations`): a superadmin works inside a professional's account to see a reported problem where it happens — no password reset, no signing the operator out. The session is minted with the auth admin API (`generateLink` + `verifyOtp`, never emailed, her own sessions untouched) into a **parallel cookie** (`@flyee/auth` `authCookieName`), so leaving is deleting a cookie, not restoring a token — there is no path that strands the operator signed out. Non-obvious constraints, all load-bearing: **(1) the write fence is in the DATABASE**, because clinical writes go from the browser straight to PostgREST and never pass through the middleware — `is_impersonated()` matches the JWT's `session_id` claim against `impersonation_sessions`, and triggers refuse clinical content, consent, patient data and AI spend while leaving settings, billing and the agenda editable. **(2) The fence never expires**: it deliberately ignores `ended_at`/`expires_at`, because a fence that lifted on expiry would silently promote a stale support session into a full-privilege session of the professional. **(3) Ending a visit uses `signOut({ scope: "local" })`** — the GoTrue default is `global`, which would sign her out of every device she owns. **(4) Starting requires the operator's own session to be AAL2**, because the impersonated session is AAL1 by construction and the middleware skips her 2FA step-up for it — the assurance is established on the operator's side instead. **(5) Credentials and `/admin` are blocked in the middleware**, not the database: password/email/2FA changes go to GoTrue, where no trigger can reach them. Transparency is part of the feature: a reason is required, she is notified in her bell, and the access is labelled as support in her own `/settings/security` log (`access_events.impersonated_by`). Duration is configurable (`platform_settings` 'impersonation' key, default 30 min). Behaviour is pinned by `packages/db/tests/0007_impersonation_fence.test.sql`.
- `/admin/insights` (`api/admin/insights/route.ts`): the model writes SQL from an `information_schema` catalog and each statement executes inside a postgres-js `sql.begin("read only", …)` transaction with a 5s `statement_timeout` — **the read-only transaction is the safety boundary, not the prompt**. Every executed query is audited and shown in the UI. Needs `DATABASE_URL` + one AI provider key; degrades to a 503 hint otherwise.
- `/admin/backups` (`@flyee/backup`): nightly Inngest cron + "Run backup now" (falls back to an inline run without Inngest keys, bounded by the function timeout). Archives land in the private `backups` bucket; downloads are service-role signed URLs.
- Real account plumbing: header bell reads the `notifications` table (create rows server-side with `lib/notifications.ts` or DB triggers — see migration 0012); announcements banner in the dashboard layout (per-user dismissal); `/settings` edits the real profile (display name + avatar → `avatars` bucket, migration 0013) and credentials (email/password); the user menu shows the real session and signs out for real.
- Floating quick-support widget (`components/support/support-widget.tsx`, mounted in both layouts) reads the superadmin-managed channels from `platform_settings` ('support' key — console at `/admin/support`, migration 0018, helper `lib/platform-settings.ts`), falling back to `BRAND.support` from `@flyee/content`; it renders nothing until a human channel (WhatsApp/email) is set.
- Cookie consent + analytics (`components/consent/cookie-consent.tsx`, mounted in both layouts; `lib/analytics.ts`): the template ships NO analytics provider, so the banner never renders (essential cookies are consent-exempt). Derived projects assign `ANALYTICS_PROVIDER` (PostHog/Plausible/GA4… behind the `AnalyticsProvider` interface) — that single assignment activates the banner, and the SDK's `init()` runs only after the user grants consent. Bump `CONSENT_VERSION` on material privacy-policy changes to re-ask. Projects needing durable acceptance records can additionally call `recordConsent` (`@flyee/audit`) for signed-in users.

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server with turbopack
- `npm run build` — production build
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting

## Auth

- Supabase via `@flyee/auth` (`client`/`server`/`middleware` entry points). `src/middleware.ts` refreshes the session and protects everything except `/` and the public prefixes (`/auth`, `/verify`, `/pricing`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/legal`).
- Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` the middleware no-ops and auth screens show a configuration hint — a fresh clone stays browsable.
- Signup metadata (`display_name`, `company`) drives profile + first organization creation in the database trigger (`packages/db/migrations/0000_init.sql`).
- **The professional's WhatsApp at sign-up** (migration `0122_signup_whatsapp_verification.sql`; `lib/signup-whatsapp.ts` + `lib/signup-whatsapp-shared.ts`; `app/auth/sign-up/{actions.ts,whatsapp-confirmation.tsx}`; `app/auth/whatsapp/`; the card in `/admin/support`). Three rules, set by the owner on 2026-10-13. **(1) The number is mandatory, always**: the form asks for it (`parseSignupWhatsApp` — a Brazilian mobile by default, any country with a leading `+`, landlines refused) and a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `auth.users` refuses every account GoTrue writes without one (`session_user = supabase_auth_admin`: public sign-up, admin API and OAuth alike), because `/signup` is callable with the public anon key and a rule that only lives in the form is no rule. **(2) Confirming it is a switch, born OFF** (`platform_settings.signup.whatsapp_confirmation`; flipped by `set_signup_whatsapp_confirmation` from the `/admin/support` card, whose server action refuses to turn it on while `signupWhatsAppMissing()` still lists an absent env var): off means the e-mail confirmation is all there is and nobody is held. **(3) With the switch on, WHEN she confirms depends on where she came from**, decided by `planSignup`: an ORDINARY sign-up shows a six-symbol code (no I/O/0/1), she sends it from her own WhatsApp to `wa.me/<WHATSAPP_SIGNUP_NUMBER>` (QR on desktop), the webhook (`confirmSignupsFromWhatsApp`) matches it and replies inside the window she opened, and only then does the browser call `signUp` with `whatsapp_verification: <token>` — the account is born confirmed; a CAMPAIGN sign-up (`buyingPlan`: `next` is `/assinatura` or `/settings/billing`) is created at once, so nothing stands between the ad and the payment, is born **pending**, and confirms afterwards at `/auth/whatsapp`. The database cannot tell a campaign from any other caller, so its rule is the general one — no confirmed token ⇒ born pending — and that is what makes the campaign path safe to open: skipping the form's confirmation buys an account that can do nothing but pay. **Where pending lives**: `account_whatsapp` (phone, `confirmation_required`, `verified_at`; CONFIRMED numbers are unique, declared ones are free text and may repeat) is the truth; a copy, `app_metadata.whatsapp_pending`, rides on the session's user so the **middleware** can hold the account without a query — anything but `/assinatura`, `/settings/billing` and the public routes redirects to `/auth/whatsapp?next=…` (API routes answer 403), which after a payment is `/onboarding`, exactly where the checkout sends her. GoTrue rewrites both metadata columns right after the insert, so one trigger strips the spent token and re-derives the flag from the truth on every metadata write (that is also how confirming clears it). Deliberate: `auth.users.phone`/`phone_confirmed_at` are never written (GoTrue derives `confirmed_at` from the latter, which would let a password sign-in skip the e-mail confirmation — FUNIL D13); `confirmation_required` is decided ONCE, at creation, so accounts from the e-mail-only period are not held when the switch turns on, and turning it OFF releases whoever was waiting (the dialog says so first); accounts older than 0122 have no row and are never held; a support (impersonated) session is never held. The checkout prefills the invoice phone from the declared number, and the accounts console shows it (`admin_accounts_overview`, recreated in 0122 with ONE changed line — any later recreation must start from that copy). Direct SQL sessions are outside the gate; tests opt in with `set local medchina.signup_gate = 'enforce'` (pinned by `packages/db/tests/0050_signup_whatsapp_verification.test.sql`, 45 assertions; the middleware's hold by `src/middleware.test.ts`; number parsing and code extraction by `src/lib/signup-whatsapp-shared.test.ts`); seeding scripts go through `scripts/signup-verification.mts`. Two things the walk against a real GoTrue taught: a sign-up or a sign-out can come back as a **504 from the gateway while GoTrue finished the job** (the client then keeps its session, or holds an error for an account that exists) — so `/auth/whatsapp` says when signing out failed instead of bouncing her back in silence, and the sign-up's retry is safe to press. Locally the number alone suffices and the message is simulated with `select public.confirm_signup_verification(array['<CODE>'], '55119…')`. OAuth stays hidden: a first Google sign-in carries no number and is refused.

## Watch out

- `src/style/global.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*` — do not recreate tokens locally.
- Deployment target is Vercel (native Next.js runtime). Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: `vercel pull/build/deploy --prebuilt` with token secrets) — the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected (multiple GitHub accounts on the owner's machine conflict with it). Runbook: `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`) must never reach client components.

===== apps/mobile/CLAUDE.md =====

# MedChina Mobile (apps/mobile)

Expo (SDK 57) + expo-router + React Native Paper — the MedChina companion app. Its product scope is CAPTURE, not review (PRD §11, docs/PRODUCT.md): consented audio recording, voice observations, resilient upload queue and processing status. NO checkout/purchase flows ever (store policy, PRD §4.4). Shares the MedChina identity with `apps/web` through `packages/*`. Before building or editing screens, load the `mobile-screen` skill; Expo/router specifics live in the `building-native-ui` skill, UX patterns in `mobile-app-ui-design`.

Expo has changed significantly across versions — see @AGENTS.md and the versioned docs it points to.

## Stack and conventions

- **Identity**: Paper MD3 themes are GENERATED from `@flyee/design-tokens` in `src/theme/index.ts` (the single MedChina Teal/Camel identity × light/dark). Never hardcode colors; dimensions come from the `native` tokens export (`RADIUS`, `MOTION`, `GRID` = 8pt grid, `TOUCH_TARGET` = 44).
- **Components**: React Native Paper first; custom components read `useTheme()`.
- **Navigation**: expo-router — routes in `app/`, `_layout.tsx` stacks, bottom `Tabs` for primary destinations, kebab-case filenames.
- **i18n**: `use-intl` with the shared catalogs from `@flyee/content/messages/*` (same keys/ICU as web's next-intl). App-shell strings live in the `mobile` namespace; locale names in `dashboard`. Every string goes through messages.
- **Auth**: `@flyee/auth/native` wired in `src/lib/supabase.ts` reading `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY`. Without env the app stays browsable with a hint (same rule as web). The session is persisted through `src/lib/session-storage.ts` — AES-GCM over AsyncStorage, key in SecureStore — because a clinical refresh token must not sit in plain text (SecureStore alone cannot hold it: >2 KB). Auto-refresh is bound to AppState (`startAutoRefresh`/`stopAutoRefresh`), the documented React Native pattern.
- **Icons**: `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` RN adapters (react-native-svg) — port more with `node scripts/port-icons.mjs ni-name` (see `src/icons/README.md`).
- **Settings**: theme mode / locale persisted in AsyncStorage (`src/providers/settings.tsx`), defaults mirror web (`system`, `pt-BR`) in `src/config.ts` — keep in sync with `apps/web/src/config.ts`.
- **Path alias**: `@/*` → `./src/*`.

## Capture flow (the app's product, PRD §11)

- Routes: `(app)/index.tsx` = **today's consultations** (the home — reads `scheduled`/`in_progress` for today; the web agenda, PRD §9.3, is what fills it), `(app)/consulta/[id].tsx` = **Modo Consulta** (hidden from the tab bar with `href: null`; its header title is set per patient).
- Data access is `src/lib/clinical.ts` (today's list, `has_active_consent`, `org_audio_allowance`). Consent is granted on the web with the patient present (PRD §9.5). On the first eligible online AI capture, the server may atomically grant the free promotional allowance; this is an operational entitlement, with no plan, price, card, renewal, checkout, purchase link or commercial trial UI in the app. When no allowance is available, the app states only that capture is unavailable; contracting remains web-only (PRD §4.4, store policy).
- **Upload queue** (`src/lib/recording-queue.ts`, PRD §11/§12.4): the audio is moved out of cache into `Paths.document/recordings` the instant recording stops, and the queue survives restarts — a bad connection must never cost a consultation. States the UI says out loud: `local` (phone only) → `uploading` → `uploaded` (server confirmed). The device copy is deleted **only after** the server confirms (HOME-SPEC §22.3). A retry resumes from where it stopped (the `recordings` row id is kept) instead of inserting twice. `blocked` = the DB guards refused (no consent / no minutes): the audio is KEPT and the reason shown — never silently discarded.
- The database is the gate, not the app: the `recordings` insert is where consent (0022) and audio allowance (0024) triggers fire; the queue reads their errors rather than re-implementing the rules.
- Recording uses `expo-audio` (`useAudioRecorder` + `RecordingPresets.HIGH_QUALITY` → `.m4a`, matching the queue's MIME); the microphone permission string is in `app.json`'s `expo-audio` plugin.
- **The capture survives the phone being put down**: `enableBackgroundRecording` (app.json) + `allowsBackgroundRecording` (`setAudioModeAsync`) keep the microphone running under the iOS `audio` background mode and an Android microphone foreground service. A consultation lasts 40–60 min with the screen auto-locking; ending the capture on `AppState !== "active"` used to truncate it silently. Only "Encerrar" (or the 2 h cap) ends a recording. If the OS kills the process anyway, `active-capture` is recovered at next launch — audio is never discarded. Both stores must be told (see `docs/STORE-REVIEW.md`).
- **A failed read is never an empty day**: `src/lib/clinical.ts` returns `offline`/`not_found`/`unavailable` explicitly and falls back to `src/lib/clinical-cache.ts` (AES-GCM over AsyncStorage, scoped to the signed-in user and to TODAY, cleared on sign-out) so a phone with no signal still opens on the day's list. Consent reads return `null` (unknown) rather than `false` — offline, the cached authorization decides and the DB stays the gate.
- **Queue states the home is honest about**: `isAwaitingDelivery` (audio on the phone, moving on its own) drives the "aguardando envio" banner; `needsAttention` (`failed`/`blocked`/`quarantined`) drives the stopped-recordings section, which lists items from ANY day — a failure from yesterday must not be buried inside yesterday's consultation. Delivered rows are purged after `DELIVERED_RETENTION_DAYS`; anything still holding audio is never purged on a timer.

## Commands

- `npm run dev:mobile` (root) or `npm start` here — Expo dev server (Expo Go first; custom builds only when native code demands).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — type check. `npx expo-doctor` — environment check.
- The capture flow's DATA contract is verified against the real database, but **microphone capture, expo-file-system and the RN upload body need a device/emulator run** — they cannot be exercised from Node.

## Boundaries (see .claude/rules/mobile-boundaries.md)

- Never import from `apps/web` — shared code lives in `packages/*` (`design-tokens`, `content`, `auth`).
- Mobile is not shrunken web: thumb-zone actions, tabs+stacks, limited type scale (≤4 sizes/2 weights per screen), ≥44pt touch targets, safe areas always.

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

- **Two design systems, chosen by what the page is FOR** (`docs/DESIGN.md`, scope note — revised 2026-08-11):
  - **Landing / offer / campaign / event pages** — anything an ad, a QR code or a WhatsApp link points at — use the **Landing DS**: the `clinical-source-home.css` global class vocabulary (`.section`, `.eyebrow`, `.button`, `.price-card`…), direct `@phosphor-icons/react` imports and hardcoded pt-BR copy. They live in a sibling route group with its own layout — `app/(funil)/` (offer/campaign/event pages: no site chrome, `noindex`) or `app/(autoridade)/` (permanent, indexed landing pages with the home's header and footer, e.g. `/china`) — or are the home itself. The marketing hooks only watch `app/(marketing)/**` and `components/marketing/**`: a Landing DS page inside `(marketing)` is BLOCKED by `marketing-lint`, and pages in `(funil)`/`(autoridade)` are never linted at all — there the page spec's checklist is the contract (`docs/DESIGN.md`, "Where the hooks do NOT look").
  - **Informational / institutional pages** (`/como-funciona`, `/recursos`, `/planos`, `/seguranca`, `/migracao`, `/sobre`, `/contato`, `/ajuda`, `/blog`, `/legal/*`) compose the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/` (`Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader`) — never hand-tuned per-page spacing/widths.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `(marketing)`, `(funil)` or `(autoridade)`. Under `(marketing)` and `components/marketing` a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; the hook does NOT fire in `(funil)`/`(autoridade)`, so load it yourself there — you never wait to be asked. On a Landing DS page, obey its conversion, copy and SEO rules, but build in the Landing DS instead of the component catalog.
- The committed visual direction lives in `docs/DESIGN.md` and is STRICT: new pages, edits and new sections INHERIT it — never re-run the direction engine or restyle the UI unless the user explicitly asks for a "redesign". Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- Every new public route must be added to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` in `apps/web/src/middleware.ts`; an INDEXED one also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`. A `noindex` page (`(funil)`, `/palestra/*`) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment — indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts` + `PUBLIC_PREFIXES`, never by the route group.
- `/help` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows, locale with EN fallback); Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx` — never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page, per the committed `docs/SEO.md`: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title — `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a localized title + description via `generateMetadata`, and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`) — never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` i18n namespace, in ALL locale files (`de,en,es,fr,pt-BR,zh-CN`) — no hardcoded strings. **Exception: Landing DS pages in `app/(funil)/**` and `app/(autoridade)/**` carry hardcoded pt-BR copy** (they speak to one market; routing campaign copy through six catalogs buys nothing and slows every edit). **The home is NOT in that exception (2026-09-18):** its copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/<locale>.ts`, six typed files with `pt-BR.ts` as the structural source of truth — editing home copy means editing all six (TypeScript refuses the build otherwise). Emphasis is inline (`**em**`, `__strong__`, `==mark==`, `\n`), rendered by `home-copy/rich.tsx`; never put JSX in a copy file.
- **Blocking on every public page, Landing DS included**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials/metrics/logos (HOME-SPEC §33.5), the clinical-safety copy guardrails, and honest scarcity — any counter or deadline must derive from server state (`docs/FUNIL.md`).
- GSAP only inside marketing client components (`Reveal`/`useGSAP`), transforms + `autoAlpha` only, honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never import GSAP in admin code.
- Site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicons) comes from `apps/web/src/brand.ts`; the logo is the single component `components/logo/logo.tsx`.

# apps/mobile boundaries

- Load the `mobile-screen` skill BEFORE creating or substantially editing screens; Expo/router specifics live in `building-native-ui`, UX patterns in `mobile-app-ui-design`.
- Never import from `apps/web`; only from `packages/*` (`@flyee/design-tokens`, `@flyee/content`, `@flyee/auth/native`).
- Visual components: React Native Paper, themed EXCLUSIVELY through `src/theme/index.ts` (generated from `@flyee/design-tokens`: `themes`, `common`, `native`, `hsl()`). Never hardcode colors or dimensions in screens.
- i18n messages come from `@flyee/content/messages/*` (shared with web); app-shell strings in the `mobile` namespace, all 6 catalogs in `packages/content/messages/` (the generated `mobile-messages/` still covers the five the app ships — parity in the source catalogs is what the tests check).
- Icons only via `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` RN adapters — port missing ones with `node scripts/port-icons.mjs`, never import an icon library directly.
- Mobile is not shrunken web: primary actions in the thumb zone, navigation via Expo Router (tabs + stacks), type scale ≤4 sizes/2 weights, touch targets ≥44pt, safe areas always.
- Features must be functionally equivalent to their web counterpart (same validation rules and i18n messages from `packages/*`), expressed in the platform's visual language.

# apps/web boundaries

- Never import from other apps (`apps/mobile` etc.). Code shared across platforms lives in `packages/*`.
- Do not redefine theme tokens locally (`--primary`, `--grey-*` etc.) — they come from `@flyee/design-tokens`.
- This is a TEMPLATE: do not introduce business logic specific to a client/derived project.
